panels.rationale: The figure displays a bulky granuloma of the larynx viewed via videolaryngoscopy. The caption explicitly states 'left laryngeal granuloma' and identifies it arising from the arytenoid, matching the definition of a posterior vocal process granuloma.

in_text_mentions: He complained of persistent dysphonia, effort dyspnea, globus sensation, and chronic throat clearing of respiratory obstruction with progressive worsening. Videolaryngoscopy demonstrated a bulky granuloma arising from the medial surface of the left arytenoid and ventricular band (Figure 1), significantly obstructing the supraglottis.

panels.rationale: The image is an endoscopic view of a granuloma-like lesion (GLL), which is being evaluated for vocal process granuloma features, and the caption specifically links this figure to a benign vascular pattern observed around the lesion.
panels.attribution_text: Klimza et al. Evaluation of narrow band imaging in the assessment of laryngeal granuloma.. Scientific reports 2019. doi:10.1038/s41598-019-50699-8. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Granuloma-like lesion with the benign vascular pattern in NBI.
in_text_mentions: Out of 47 patients, who presented with GLL, 13/47 (28%) (group A) had perpendicular vascular changes visualized in NBI on the mucosa surrounding granulation tissue (Fig. 1). The remaining 34/47 (72%) (group B) had longitudinal vascular changes on mucosa surrounding GLL (Fig. 2). In all patients, the microvascular pattern in NBI was compared with the final histology.Figure 1Granuloma-like lesion with the suspicious vascular pattern in NBI.Figure 2Granuloma-like lesion with the benign vascular pattern in NBI.
